name: Jamie Oliver's Chicken in Milk {Seriously Delish}

ingredients.buy: 3 whole chickens, about 3 3/4 lb each (11 1/2 lb total)
2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
scant 1 cup loosely packed fresh sage leaves

writer_notes: All 9 locked ingredients are used by a step: chicken, salt, black pepper (season); olive oil (brown); ground cinnamon, fresh sage, lemon zest, garlic, milk (added to pot before baking). No orphans, nothing invented.

BUILD DIVERGES FROM SOURCE ON CINNAMON: source transcription says '1/2 stick cinnamon' but the locked build buys '1 3/4 teaspoons ground cinnamon'. Method was written around ground cinnamon as bought. Flagged for QA.
Scaled from a single 3 to 3.5 lb bird to three whole chickens for 14 servings; browning and baking may need a large pot or batching, which the method calls out.
Macro mentions written as tokens {{cal}} and {{protein}}; carbs kept qualitative ('barely any carbs') to avoid a stray literal. Cost as ${{cost_ps}}.

Only shop_smart package claim is milk: 8 cups needed = exactly half a gallon, so one gallon jug covers it. Traces to the Milk buy line, not a price claim. No per-ounce or per-batch economics claimed because no cost_lines were in dispatch.
'Do not strain the sauce' is faithful to the source's final instruction (keep the curds, garlic, and sage on the chicken).

prose.intro_html: Jamie Oliver called this one seriously delish, and for once the internet did not oversell it. Chicken braised in milk sounds like a mistake right up until you taste it. The milk breaks down into soft little curds, the lemon zest and garlic melt into it, and you end up with a sauce that has no business coming from five plain ingredients. We scaled it up to three whole chickens so it feeds a full week of dinners instead of one nice Sunday. At {{cal}} calories, {{protein}} grams of protein, and barely any carbs per serving, it lands right where a high protein dinner is supposed to land. Let me walk you through it.
prose.shop_smart:
• Buy whole chickens. A whole bird is the cheapest chicken you can put in a cart per pound, and this batch wants three of them at roughly 3 3/4 pounds each. Buy them skin on. That skin is where the browning flavor comes from, so do not let anyone talk you into skinless.
  • One gallon of milk does the job. The recipe needs 8 cups, which is exactly half a gallon, so a single gallon jug of low fat milk covers it with plenty left over for the fridge.
  • Fresh sage, one package. A scant cup of loosely packed leaves is about what comes in one small clamshell of fresh sage at most stores. Buy the fresh, not the dried, for this one.
  • Lemons for zest only. You are buying 7 lemons for their zest, so pick firm, heavy ones with taut skin. Zest them, then keep the naked lemons for water, dressing, or squeezing over dinner.
  • Garlic goes in whole. The cloves stay in their skins, so a few heads of garlic gets you to 35 cloves with zero peeling. Less knife work for you.
  • Check your pantry first. Ground cinnamon, salt, black pepper, and olive oil are things most kitchens already stock, so you may only be buying the chicken, milk, sage, lemons, and garlic.
prose.make_it:
1. Heat your oven to 375F. Pat the chickens dry all over with paper towels so the skin can actually brown.
  2. Season them well. Sprinkle the salt and plenty of black pepper over each bird and pat it all over, paying attention to the top and the sides.
  3. Heat the olive oil in a heavy based pot over high heat. Brown the chicken all over as best you can, tilting and turning it to catch as much skin as possible. With three birds you will want a big pot, or work one at a time and brown them in turns.
  4. Pour off the excess fat. Tip it carefully out of the pot with the chicken still inside if you can manage it, or lift the chicken onto a plate, drain the fat, and set the bird back in.
  5. Add the rest of the cast to the pot with the chicken: the ground cinnamon, the sage leaves, the lemon zest, the whole skin on garlic cloves, and the milk. Do not worry that the milk looks strange. That is the whole trick.
  6. Bake it covered for 40 minutes, then uncovered for 50 minutes, about an hour and a half in total. The milk will split into those golden curds you are after.
  7. Let it stand about 5 minutes, then lift the chicken out onto a board. Do not strain the sauce. You want the curds, the soft garlic, and the bits of sage right there on the plate.
prose.portion_html: This one comes apart easy. Pull all the chicken off the bones while it is still warm, skin and all, and give the meat a rough chop or shred. Weigh your empty container, then weigh the full pot of meat, and divide the total across the 14 containers so every one gets the same honest portion. Spoon the sauce over each, curds and garlic and sage included, and you have 14 dinners that reheat like a dream. If a couple of containers run a little light on meat, even them out with an extra ladle of that sauce.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is the part that matters. At ${{cost_ps}} a serving, you are eating a Jamie Oliver dinner for less than most people spend without thinking twice. Three whole chickens is the cheapest way to get {{protein}} grams of protein onto a plate, and the milk, garlic, sage, and lemon are pennies sitting next to the bird. Cook it once, eat it all week, and let the arithmetic do the bragging.

head.description: Jamie Oliver's Chicken in Milk scaled for meal prep: three whole chickens braised in milk with garlic, sage, lemon zest, and cinnamon for 14 high protein dinners at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein each.
head.keywords: chicken in milk, Jamie Oliver chicken in milk, meal prep chicken, high protein dinner, whole chicken recipe, budget meal prep, braised chicken, low carb chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 375F and pat the chickens dry all over with paper towels.
Season the chickens with the salt and black pepper, patting it over the top and sides.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over high heat and brown the chickens all over, working in batches if needed.
Pour off the excess fat from the pot, lifting the chicken out first if that is easier.
Add the ground cinnamon, sage leaves, lemon zest, whole garlic cloves, and milk to the pot with the chicken.
Bake covered for 40 minutes, then uncovered for 50 minutes, about an hour and a half total.
Rest 5 minutes, then lift out the chicken and serve with the unstrained sauce.
Pull the meat off the bones, divide evenly across 14 containers by weight, and spoon the sauce over each.
